main_text.l: Fac sis, quoad eius fieri potest, αὐτάρκως [?] τῷ τρόπῳ [?] τῶν, tua contentus forte, humilia aut mediocria ne afperneris. Si enim a teipso primum proftratus non fueris: minus deinde periculi tibi erit ab externis illis molestijs, quas qui magna ex parte tanquam alienas excludunt, minus laborant, quàm ij, qui tanta laborant animi impotentia, vt conuicia vana, quibus fe notari vident, no posfint contemnere: ut dispendio exiguo nolint auream redimere pacem. Sed de his alias quoque dicam.
SED, INQVAM, QVID TVM FA-ciam, si me inhumanissime, ab ijs quibus cum coniunctissime uixeram, nullo meo malo merito, tractari uideam?

Quid aliud facias, quàm vt mentis tuae oculis in Deum direftis, primum dicas: Ta-cui, quia tu fecisti Domine, Psal 39.10. Quo-modo enim nō optimum tibi fuerit, quòd à proprio Deo Domino q; tuo factum intelligis? Vidit ille tibi hac ferula opus fuisse, i-deo e te castigauit. Erit igitur religiosę prudentiae tuae, cauffas eius rei inuestigare. Ni-hil autem dubium est, προνοητικῶν [?] causam esse, quòd nimium hominibus illis, minus autem quàm par esset, Deo tuo deferres: πρό-

page.notes: The Greek words in the first line ("αὐτάρκως", "τῷ τρόπῳ", "τῶν") are uncertain; the scan is faint and the letters are not clearly legible, so they are marked [?]. The Greek word after "est," (read as προνοητικῶν) is also doubtful. The catchword "πρό-" at the foot is partly legible. The sentence "SED, INQVAM..." is set in spaced capitals and is treated as a quoted objection, not a heading, so it is written as a paragraph. The hyphen in "FA-ciam" is printed at the line end and kept. The printed "pri-mum" at the start of the second line of the first paragraph shows a damaged dot; it is read as "primum". Nothing else on the page is damaged.
